title_en: Yang Shuling v. Ping An Property Insurance Company of China, Ltd., Tianjin Baodi Branch — dispute over insurance contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. Terms such as 'family members,' 'lineal blood relatives,' and 'relatives' are all legal concepts, and insurance companies engaged in the insurance business have no right to arbitrarily interpret the aforementioned legal concepts. 'Family' is legally equivalent to 'household registration,' and 'family members' refer to persons who permanently live together under the same household registration, with each member's economic income serving as common property of the family. 'Family members' and 'lineal blood relatives' or 'relatives' are not the same concept; persons who are lineal blood relatives are not necessarily family members of each other.

full_text_en:
Yang Shuling v. China Ping An Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Tianjin Baodi Branch — Dispute over Insurance Contract

Ruling Summary

1. "Family members," "lineal relatives by blood," and "relatives" are all legal concepts, and an insurance company engaged in the insurance business has no right to interpret these legal concepts arbitrarily. "Family" is legally equivalent to "household registration," and "family members" refer to persons who permanently live together under the same household registration, with each member's economic income constituting the common property of the family. "Family members" is not the same concept as "lineal relatives by blood" or "relatives"; persons who have a lineal blood relationship are not necessarily family members of each other.

2. Pursuant to Article 18 of the Insurance Law, if an insurance contract contains a clause regarding the insurer's exemption from liability, the insurer shall, at the time of concluding the contract, provide a clear explanation to the applicant. If no such clear explanation is given, the clause shall be invalid. The term "clear explanation" means that, before or at the time of signing the insurance contract with the applicant, the insurer shall, in addition to drawing the applicant's attention to the exemption clause on the insurance policy, also explain the concept, content, and legal consequences of the relevant exemption clause to the applicant or its agent in written or oral form, so that the applicant understands the true meaning and legal consequences of the clause.

Plaintiff: Yang Shuling, male, 32 years old, farmer, residing in Dachenzhuang Village, Dazhongzhuang Town, Baodi District, Tianjin.

Defendant: China Ping An Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Tianjin Baodi Branch, domiciled at Nanguan Street, Baodi District, Tianjin.

Responsible Person: Dong Xiaohua, Manager of the Branch.

The plaintiff, Yang Shuling, filed a lawsuit with the People's Court of Baodi District, Tianjin, against the defendant, China Ping An Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Tianjin Baodi Branch (hereinafter referred to as "Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch"), regarding a dispute over an insurance contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On January 20, 2006, the plaintiff applied to the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, for comprehensive third-party liability insurance for a motor vehicle. On the same day, the defendant accepted the plaintiff's application and issued an insurance policy. The insurance contract stipulated that the insurance period was from January 21, 2006 to January 20, 2007, the premium was RMB 1,386.60, and the sum insured was RMB 50,000. At approximately 9:00 p.m. on March 17, 2006, while driving the insured vehicle, the plaintiff negligently knocked down a wall, causing the death of his mother, Zhang Yurong. On April 11 of the same year, through mediation by the Traffic Police Brigade of the Tianjin Public Security Bureau Baodi Branch, the plaintiff made corresponding compensation for the accident damages. After the accident was resolved through mediation, the plaintiff filed an insurance claim with the defendant, which was refused. According to the insurance policy, the defendant could be exempted from 20% of the liability. Therefore, the plaintiff petitioned the court to order the defendant to pay insurance compensation of RMB 40,000 and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The plaintiff, Yang Shuling, submitted the following evidence:

1. A motor vehicle insurance policy, to prove that the plaintiff, as the applicant, and the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, as the insurer, had formed an insurance contract relationship regarding the insured motor vehicle involved;
2. A traffic accident recognition certificate issued by the Traffic Police Brigade of the Tianjin Public Security Bureau Baodi Branch on March 28, 2006, to prove that on the afternoon of March 17, 2006, the plaintiff was involved in a traffic accident while driving the insured vehicle, causing the death of his mother;
3. A mediation agreement for damages from the traffic accident dated April 11, 2006, to prove that the plaintiff had made corresponding compensation for the traffic accident involved;
4. Two household registration booklets, to prove that the plaintiff had separated from his parents and lived independently, belonging to two different household registrations.

Defendant's Defense: According to the terms of the insurance contract, if the vehicle driven by the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, caused casualties to his family members, the defendant should be exempted from liability. The "family members" referred to in the insurance contract include the insured's lineal relatives by blood and other relatives living together with them. The deceased in this case was the plaintiff's mother, who is a lineal relative by blood of the plaintiff. Therefore, when the plaintiff drove the insured vehicle and caused an accident resulting in his mother's death, the defendant should be exempted from liability. The exemption clause in the insurance contract was clearly indicated in bold typeface, and the plaintiff fully understood and accepted it. Therefore, the defendant disagreed with the plaintiff's claims.

The defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, submitted to the court on the same day the "Motor Vehicle Insurance Clauses and Interpretations" (Baodian Fa [2000] No. 102) dated June 15, 2000, and the "Notice on the Abolition of Certain Regulatory Documents" (Baodian Fa [2005] No. 18) dated February 24, 2005, to prove that Baodian Fa [2000] No. 102 had become invalid and to demonstrate the legal basis for the company's handling of insurance claims related to the traffic accident in this case.

The court of first instance organized both parties to conduct cross-examination and authentication.

Regarding the authenticity and legality of Evidence 1 and Evidence 4 submitted by the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, raised no objection but argued that the insurance contract had already clearly informed the plaintiff of the insurer's exemption clause. Whether the plaintiff had separated from his parents and lived independently or belonged to two different household registrations did not affect the fact that he and his parents were family members of each other. The defendant had no objection to Evidence 2 submitted by the plaintiff. The defendant argued that Evidence 3 submitted by the plaintiff was a photocopy, the authenticity and legality of which could not be confirmed, and that this evidence was irrelevant to the case.

Regarding the evidence submitted by the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, the plaintiff argued that even if Baodian Fa [2000] No. 102 had become invalid, the provisions on "family members" in that document were reasonable and should apply to this case.

The People's Court of Baodi District, Tianjin, found the following facts in the first instance:

On January 20, 2006, the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, applied to the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, for comprehensive third-party liability insurance for a motor vehicle. The insured vehicle was a Jin AA9251 Shidai light truck. On the same day, the defendant accepted the plaintiff's application and issued an insurance policy. The insurance contract stipulated that the plaintiff was the insured, the defendant was the insurer, the insurance period was from January 21, 2006 to January 20, 2007, the premium was RMB 1,386.60, and the sum insured was RMB 50,000. Article 3, Chapter 2, Part 2 of the insurance contract provides: "In the event that the insured vehicle causes the following personal injury or death, regardless of whether the insured is legally liable for compensation, the insurer shall not be liable for compensation: (1) The insured or a driver permitted by the insured, and their family members..." Article 22, Part 4, Definitions, of the insurance contract provides: "Family members include the insured's lineal relatives by blood and other relatives living together with them." Article 4(2) of Part 3, Occupant Liability Insurance Clause, provides: "According to the degree of responsibility borne by the driver of the insured vehicle in the accident, the occupant liability insurance shall apply an accident liability exemption rate within the amount that meets the compensation provisions. For full responsibility, a 20% exemption shall apply..." At approximately 9:00 p.m. on March 17, 2006, while driving the insured vehicle, the plaintiff negligently knocked down a wall, causing the death of his mother, Zhang Yurong. On March 28 of the same year, the Traffic Police Brigade of the Tianjin Public Security Bureau Baodi Branch issued a traffic accident recognition certificate, finding the plaintiff fully responsible for the traffic accident. On April 11 of the same year, through mediation by the Traffic Police Brigade of the Tianjin Public Security Bureau Baodi Branch, the plaintiff made corresponding compensation for the damages from the traffic accident. After the accident was resolved through mediation, the plaintiff filed an insurance claim with the defendant, but the defendant refused to settle the claim.

It was further found that the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, had separated from his parents and lived independently, and did not belong to the same household registration as his parents.

The issue in dispute in this case was whether the insurer's exemption clause in the insurance contract signed between the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, and the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, was valid, and whether the defendant should settle the insurance claim for the damages from the traffic accident involved.

Opinion of the Court (First Instance):

An insurance contract is an agreement between the applicant and the insurer to establish the rights and obligations of the insurance relationship. The motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract entered into between the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, and the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, was lawful and valid and should be protected by law. After the plaintiff paid the premium as agreed, a traffic accident occurred, and a mediation agreement for compensation was reached with the opposing party of the accident. The plaintiff's losses were supported by evidence. The defendant refused to compensate the plaintiff based on the following content from the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract involved: "In the event that the insured vehicle causes the following personal injury or death, regardless of whether the insured is legally liable for compensation, the insurer shall not be liable for compensation: (1) The insured or a driver permitted by the insured, and their family members..." and "Family members include the insured's lineal relatives by blood and other relatives living together with them." Relying on these provisions, the defendant argued that the plaintiff caused a traffic accident while driving the insured vehicle, resulting in his mother's death, and that the plaintiff and his mother were family members of each other. Therefore, the traffic accident in question fell within the scope of the insurer's exemption clause, and the defendant had reason to be exempted from liability. On this point, the court held that the defendant's defense was untenable. Although the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract signed between the plaintiff and the defendant was lawful and valid, the insurer's exemption clause was invalid, and the defendant should settle the insurance claim for the damages from the traffic accident involved.

1. The insurance contract in question had no legal basis for excluding the plaintiff's (Yang Shuling's) mother from the scope of third-party liability insurance coverage.

First, the insurance contract in question was a motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract. According to common understanding and internationally accepted insurance concepts, a "third party" in motor vehicle third-party liability insurance refers to all persons other than the two parties to the insurance contract, i.e., the insurer and the insured (including persons inside the insured vehicle). The purpose of motor vehicle third-party liability insurance is to ensure that third parties can obtain relief from the insurer when they suffer damages due to a traffic accident, thereby protecting the interests of unspecified third parties. A motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract is an aleatory contract; whether the insurer should pay insurance benefits depends on the occurrence of a contingent event, i.e., a traffic accident, after the contract is formed. In this case, the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, knocked down a courtyard wall while driving, causing his mother's death. The occurrence of this traffic accident was purely accidental. As a victim of the traffic accident involved, the plaintiff's mother was no different from any other third party who, under normal circumstances, has no lineal blood relationship or other kinship with the perpetrator of the traffic accident. In the absence of clear provisions in existing laws and regulations, the relevant standardized exemption clause in the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract that excluded family members of the insured or the driver of the insured vehicle artificially and deliberately narrowed the scope of third parties. The establishment of this standardized exemption clause was primarily aimed at protecting the insurer's interests, which ran counter to the original intention of establishing motor vehicle third-party liability insurance. The motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract in question was a standard form contract drafted in advance by the insurer. The provider of such a standard form contract should adhere to the principle of good faith. Article 39 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law") provides: "Where standard terms are adopted in concluding a contract, the party supplying the standard terms shall determine the rights and obligations between the parties in accordance with the principle of fairness..." Article 40 of the Contract Law provides: "...Standard terms that exempt the supplier from its liability, increase the other party's liability, or exclude the other party's main rights shall be void." Accordingly, the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, used its advantageous position to preset standardized exemption clauses to narrow the scope of third parties and maximize the exemption of its own liability. This had no legal basis, and the standardized exemption clause should be deemed invalid.

Second, the content in the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract to the effect that "family members include the insured's lineal relatives by blood and other relatives living together with them" constituted an invalid interpretation that violated the law. "Family members," "lineal relatives by blood," and "relatives" are all legal concepts. The defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, as an economic entity engaged in the insurance business, had no right to interpret these legal concepts arbitrarily. According to the relevant laws and regulations of our country, a "family" in the legal sense is equivalent to a household registration; one family is one household, and one household is one family. "Family members" refer to persons who permanently live together under the same household registration, with each member's economic income constituting the common property of the family. Therefore, "family members" is not the same concept as "lineal relatives by blood" or "relatives"; persons who have a lineal blood relationship are not necessarily family members of each other. Based on the facts of this case, the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, had separated from his parents and lived independently, belonging to two different household registrations, and their finances and daily lives were independent. Therefore, although the plaintiff's mother was a lineal relative by blood of the plaintiff, she was not a family member of the plaintiff. Consequently, even if the standardized exemption clause in the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract to the effect that "the insurer shall not be liable for compensation for personal injury or death caused by the insured vehicle to the insured or a driver permitted by the insured, and their family members, regardless of whether the insured is legally liable for compensation" was valid, the clause should not apply to exempt the insurer from liability because the plaintiff's mother was not a family member of the plaintiff.

2. The defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, failed to fulfill its obligation to provide a "clear explanation" regarding the standardized exemption clause, and therefore the standardized exemption clause was invalid.

Article 18 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Insurance Law") provides: "If an insurance contract contains a clause regarding the insurer's exemption from liability, the insurer shall, at the time of concluding the contract, provide a clear explanation to the applicant. If no such clear explanation is given, the clause shall not be effective." The defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, argued that when it provided the text of the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract involved, it had clearly indicated the exemption clause in bold typeface, and therefore it should be deemed to have fulfilled its obligation to provide a "clear explanation." According to the "Reply on How to Understand the 'Clear Explanation' Stipulated in Article 17 of the Insurance Law" issued by the Supreme People's Court on January 21, 2000 (the "Insurance Law" referred to here is the Insurance Law before amendment; the provisions of Article 17 of the Insurance Law before amendment are consistent with those of Article 18 of the current Insurance Law), the term "clear explanation" means that, before or at the time of signing the insurance contract with the applicant, the insurer shall, in addition to drawing the applicant's attention to the exemption clause on the insurance policy, also explain the concept, content, and legal consequences of the relevant exemption clause to the applicant or its agent in written or oral form, so that the applicant understands the true meaning and legal consequences of the clause. An insurance contract is a contract with relatively strong professional content, involving many professional terms. Applicants, especially farmers like the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, in this case, often do not have a thorough understanding of them, making it even more incumbent upon the insurer to provide a clear explanation. The defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, by indicating the exemption clause in bold typeface in the text of the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract involved, merely fulfilled its obligation to draw the applicant's attention. Based on the facts and evidence of this case, it could not be determined that Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch had fulfilled its obligation to provide a clear explanation of the concept, content, and legal consequences of the exemption clause in written or oral form to the applicant or its agent, so that the applicant understood the true meaning and legal consequences of the clause. Therefore, the exemption clause stipulated in the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract involved should be deemed invalid.

In summary, the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, relied on the standardized exemption clause in the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract involved to refuse to settle the insurance claim for the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, which was inconsistent with the law and was not supported. Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch failed to perform its obligations under the insurance contract, causing the dispute, and should bear full responsibility. According to the provisions of the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract involved, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch could be exempted from 20% of the sum insured of RMB 50,000. Yang Shuling's claim for an order that Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch pay insurance compensation of RMB 40,000 had factual and legal basis and should be upheld.

Accordingly, on August 16, 2006, the People's Court of Baodi District, Tianjin, rendered the following judgment:

The defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, shall pay the plaintiff, Yang Shuling, insurance compensation of RMB 40,000.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 2,948 shall be borne by the defendant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch.

Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, dissatisfied with the judgment of the first instance, filed an appeal with the First Intermediate People's Court of Tianjin. The main grounds of appeal were: 1. The motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract signed between the appellee, Yang Shuling, and the appellant clearly defined the rights and obligations of both parties. The appellee did not raise any objection to the standardized exemption clause in the contract at the time of signing, nor did he apply to revoke it during the performance of the contract. 2. An insurance company does not compensate for all risks that occur to the subject matter insured, but rather defines the specific scope of risks covered based on the corresponding premium. The exemption clause in an insurance contract is a specific definition of the scope of insured risk from an extension perspective and is a unique expression of insurance products. It is not an unfair clause under the Contract Law that exempts one party's liability and increases the other party's liability. 3. Current laws, regulations, and relevant insurance regulatory policies of our country do not explicitly define the scope of "third party" in motor vehicle third-party liability insurance. The insurance company, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the national insurance regulatory authority, excludes the insured's family members from the third party, which is not illegal. 4. Excluding the insured's family members from the third party has a certain degree of reasonableness. Under a system of community property, if one family member causes injury to another due to an accident or negligence, the civil compensation liability borne by one party is equivalent to using part of the community property to compensate the community property itself, which has no practical significance and is inconsistent with the principle of indemnity in compensation concepts. 5. The appellant had fulfilled its obligation to provide a clear explanation regarding the standardized exemption clause in the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract involved. The court of first instance, relying on the "Reply on How to Understand the 'Clear Explanation' Stipulated in Article 17 of the Insurance Law" issued by the Supreme People's Court, erred in finding that the appellant failed to fulfill its clear explanation obligation. That Reply was made in response to an individual case, is not a judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court, does not have universal applicability, and cannot serve as the legal basis for adjudicating this case. In conclusion, the appellant requested the revocation of the first-instance judgment, a remand for retrial, or a modified judgment dismissing the appellee's claims.

Appellee Yang Shuling argued: 1. According to the *Provisions and Interpretations on Motor Vehicle Insurance Clauses* (Baoshanfa [2000] No. 102) issued on June 15, 2000, "family members" under the insurance contract can be distinguished based on the concept of a household with independent finances. Accordingly, family members should refer to members of each household registration, and should not be determined solely by lineal blood relationships or other kinship ties. This interpretation is consistent with the principles of insurance contract interpretation and with relevant Chinese laws and regulations. Therefore, although this interpretation has been repealed, it should be applied by reference until new relevant laws and regulations are enacted. The appellee and his parents have separate households, are not under the same household registration, and are financially independent; they are not family members of each other. Consequently, the standardized exclusion clause in the third-party liability insurance contract for the motor vehicle in question, which excludes the appellee's mother from the definition of "third party," has no legal basis and is also contrary to common sense. 2. The appellant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, failed to fulfill its duty to clearly explain the standardized exclusion clause in the third-party liability insurance contract for the motor vehicle in question. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Understand the "Clear Explanation" Stipulated in Article 17 of the Insurance Law is consistent with Article 18 of the current Insurance Law and Article 39 of the Contract Law and should also be applied by reference. In conclusion, the appellee requests that this Court reject the appellant's appeal and affirm the judgment of the first instance.

Neither the appellant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, nor the appellee, Yang Shuling, submitted any new evidence.

The Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance upon review.

Opinion of the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court on appeal:

The appellee, Yang Shuling, insured his motor vehicle with the appellant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch, for third-party liability insurance and paid the relevant premium. The insurance contract relationship between the parties was established. The third-party liability insurance contract for the motor vehicle in question is lawful and valid, and both parties to the contract should perform their obligations accordingly. The provisions in the contract stating that "the insurer shall not be liable for any bodily injury to the insured, the insured's permitted driver, or their family members caused by the insured vehicle, regardless of whether the insured is legally liable for such injury," and the interpretation in the contract that "family members include the insured's lineal blood relatives and other relatives living together," both constitute standardized exclusion clauses. The insurer providing such a standardized contract is legally obligated to clearly explain these exclusion clauses to the insured. According to the *Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Understand the 'Clear Explanation' Stipulated in Article 17 of the Insurance Law*, the so-called "clear explanation" means that before or at the time of concluding the insurance contract, the insurer, in addition to drawing the proposer's attention to the exclusion clauses in the insurance policy, must also explain the concepts, content, and legal consequences of the relevant exclusion clauses to the proposer or their agent, in writing or orally, so that the proposer understands the true meaning and legal consequences of the clauses. Although this Reply was made regarding Article 17 of the pre-amendment Insurance Law, the provisions of Article 17 of the pre-amendment Insurance Law are consistent with Article 18 of the current Insurance Law. Furthermore, although this Reply was made for a specific case, people's courts may refer to it when adjudicating similar cases. Insurance contracts are highly specialized and involve numerous technical terms; the insurer has a duty to provide clear explanations to the proposer. Although Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch highlighted the exclusion clauses in bold type in the text of the motor vehicle third-party liability insurance contract, this merely fulfilled its obligation to remind the proposer to pay attention. Based on the facts and evidence of this case, it cannot be determined that Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch fulfilled its duty to clearly explain the concepts, content, and legal consequences of the exclusion clauses to the proposer or his agent in writing or orally, so as to enable the proposer to understand the true meaning and legal consequences of those clauses. Therefore, regardless of whether the standardized exclusion clause regarding "bodily injury to the insured, the insured's permitted driver, or their family members caused by the insured vehicle" and the interpretation that "family members include the insured's lineal blood relatives and other relatives living together" in the third-party liability insurance contract have a legal basis or are valid, such standardized exclusion clauses are rendered invalid because the appellant failed to fulfill its duty of clear explanation, and the exclusion clauses have no binding effect on the appellee. The appellant's grounds for appeal are insufficient and are not supported.

Accordingly, the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 152 and Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on October 25, 2006:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 2,948 shall be borne by the appellant, Ping An Insurance Baodi Branch.

This judgment is final.
